comparator: United States packaged consumer products after PE buyouts
sector: Consumer packaged goods sold through grocery, drug, and mass-merchandiser channels
finding: NBER study uses monthly store-level prices and unit sales for nearly two million products in about 43,000 US locations from 2006-2016 and links 236 target companies to PE acquisitions. It finds revenue growth after PE buyouts; average product-line prices rise about 5 percent, but the same existing product in the same store rises only about 1 percent relative to competitors, implying mix/geography/new-product effects matter.
why_it_matters_for_india: Directly relevant to India packaged-food claims because PE can affect SKU mix, premiumization, geographic expansion, and product launches even when same-product prices do not rise sharply.
transferability_limits: US retail scanner data, product categories, retailer bargaining and income geography differ from India; this does not prove Haldiram, Balaji, Theobroma, or Capital Foods effects.

finding: Earlier working-paper version reports 2.7 percent average category-level price increases relative to matched firms, while later discussion emphasizes that category-level price increases can reflect higher-priced new products or upmarket composition rather than simple same-UPC price hikes.
why_it_matters_for_india: Useful for correcting repository-style use of a single price number: the mechanism matters as much as the average estimate.
transferability_limits: Working-paper versions differ; use the newer NBER framing for final inference and avoid treating 2.7 percent as a universal PE price effect.

finding: Chevalier's Journal of Finance abstract reports that supermarket prices rose after LBOs where rivals were also highly leveraged, while prices fell where rivals had low leverage and concentrated markets, suggesting rival financial structure and local competition condition outcomes.
why_it_matters_for_india: Shows that financial leverage and local competition can change food-price outcomes; PE effects are not uniform across markets.
confidence: High for classic study; abstract-only in current file
transferability_limits: Older US supermarket context; full text not locally available; India quick-commerce and kirana dynamics are different.

finding: Bernstein and Sheen's restaurant study reports improved health inspection outcomes after PE buyouts, lower menu prices, lower employee headcount, and lower store-closure likelihood in Florida restaurant chains.
why_it_matters_for_india: Counterbalances confirmation bias: PE can improve operations in some food-service contexts while also changing labor inputs.
transferability_limits: Restaurant chains and health inspections are not the same as packaged foods, grocery, quick commerce, or Indian QSRs; external validity is limited.

sector: Food chain from producers to retail
finding: OECD cautions that low profit margins in food-chain stages do not prove absence of market power, but they limit simple claims that one actor can raise farmgate prices without raising consumer prices or taking losses. It emphasizes data limitations and chain-specific price/margin analysis.
why_it_matters_for_india: Important for India farmer-harm claims: buyer power must be tested with crop/channel-specific farmgate, wholesale, retail, and margin data rather than inferred from ownership changes.
transferability_limits: OECD examples are mostly Europe/advanced economies; India has MSPs, mandis, fragmented retail, informal markets and platform growth.

comparator: Safeway-Albertsons merger and California specialty crops
sector: Food retail M&A and upstream producers
finding: Study of the 2014 Safeway-Albertsons acquisition finds specialty crop growers interviewed viewed retail M&A unfavorably, citing uncertainty, lower prices, lost revenue and higher transaction costs; quantitative evidence indicated lower prices received and higher volatility in relevant settings.
why_it_matters_for_india: Provides a concrete upstream producer mechanism: retail buyer consolidation can affect growers through bargaining power and transaction costs.
transferability_limits: This is a US retail merger, not PE-specific India evidence; sample is specialty crops and partly qualitative.
